qt: to the Commission Klára Dobrev (S&D) Subject:

The integration of generative AI into widely used digital services raises concerns about educational institutions’ ability to choose which technologies children use. Where Google Search’s AI functionalities cannot be disabled independently of traditional search, schools may face a choice between accepting unwanted AI features and abandoning an established service. This raises broader internal market and procurement concerns about purchasers’ control over service changes, supplier dependence and access for alternative providers, including for European small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). 1.

How does the Commission assess the adequacy of EU public procurement rules in protecting educational authorities when suppliers introduce generative AI into existing digital services without an independently configurable, AI-free option?

Will the Commission develop guidance or model procurement clauses which would enable educational authorities to require independent control over AI features, interoperability, data portability and effective exit options throughout the duration of a contract?

What concrete measures will the Commission take to reduce supplier dependence in educational digital infrastructure and to improve market access for European SMEs offering interoperable, child-safe alternatives, while respecting Member States’ responsibility for education?
